## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`refresh_fingerprints` should be fixed: it overwrites the fingerprints of files that are already tracked. If a tracked file was edited by hand and is passed to `refresh_fingerprints`, verification no longer detects the edit, which breaks the integrity guarantee the description promises.

## Changes
The pull request adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py` so that new files can be added to the JSON fingerprint manifest. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py`, which covers both helpers.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Keep existing fingerprints in refresh_fingerprints — If you call `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])` after `tracked.txt` was edited by hand, line 17 replaces the stored digest with the edited file's digest, so `verify` then returns True. The test at `tests/test_integrity.py:6` passes only an unedited tracked file, so it cannot detect this. — An integrity check that should fail on tampered tracked files passes after any refresh that names them, so the tampering goes unnoticed. — Fix: Skip names already in `entries`, as `register_new_files` does at `app/integrity.py:24`, and extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` with an edited tracked file.
